subject: Usage attribution snapshot and tax evidence chain
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: usage attribution snapshot + EU VAT evidence

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the sync last week. Our finance team has flagged a discrepancy between the usage we see in Redwood's marketplace payout ledger and the invoice you received for Feb 2027. Specifically, there are several high-volume usage lines that appear to have been attributed to Acme UK (VAT-registered) and Acme EU (non-VAT entity) at different timestamps; that mix affects how VAT should be remitted.

Can you please share: 1) a per-merchant usage export for Feb 2027 (timestamped events, usage_id, SKU, buyer_entity_id) and 2) any marketplace evidence Acme has that shows which legal entity was charged at the time of the transaction?

Attaching a short snapshot from our side (redwood-ledger-sample.csv) that highlights the three suspect usage_ids. If you can push your export by EOD Wed (your time) we can run a side-by-side reconciliation and propose a corrective invoice or credit memo if needed.

Appreciate it — Chloe

--
Chloe Martin
Sr. Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
(415) 555-0132

From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme-corp.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 13:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: usage attribution snapshot + EU VAT evidence

Chloe —

Thanks for the note and for the sample. Attached is the per-merchant export from our side (acme-usage-snapshot-2027-02.csv). The marketplace (AWS MP) provided the consumption report and our procurement systems map most events to the Acme UK VAT entity, but I see a small batch where the buyer_entity_id is blank — that typically happened during the marketplace cutover we ran 2027-02-28 22:40 UTC.

We're pulling supporting docs from procurement (POs and entity mappings) and will send by EOD Wednesday. In the meantime, I flagged the three usage_ids you called out — they show as billed on 2027-02-28 23:02 UTC from the marketplace feed.

Alice

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 07:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: usage attribution snapshot + EU VAT evidence

Chloe / Jonas —

I pulled the full Feb ledger and attached the ledger grab (redwood-ledger-snapshot-2027-02.xlsx). Early observations:
- There is a window 2027-02-28T22:30:00Z -> 2027-03-01T00:15:00Z with a spike in delayed event ingestion from the marketplace connector.
- During that window several usage events lack buyer_entity_id in our canonical table; the marketplace feed did include a marketplace_billing_entity which in most cases maps to Acme UK.
- A subset of events were reprocessed and re-emitted with different timestamps (origin_ts vs processed_ts mismatch).

I think we need to provide Acme with: a) origin-level event export (raw marketplace CSV), b) our processed ledger rows, and c) a reconciliation of origin -> processed (showing reprocessed event IDs).

I've attached the ledger snapshot. Jonas, can you run the event-level diff and confirm whether reprocessed events preserve the original usage_id? If they don't, we need to surface that to Acme and coordinate on a corrective invoice.

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Revenue Ops & Billing
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 10:21:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Request: usage attribution snapshot + EU VAT evidence

On Wed, 03 Mar 2027 07:08:00 -0700 Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> I pulled the full Feb ledger and attached the ledger grab (redwood-ledger-snapshot-2027-02.xlsx). Early observations:
> - There is a window 2027-02-28T22:30:00Z -> 2027-03-01T00:15:00Z with a spike in delayed event ingestion from the marketplace connector.

I ran an event-diff and here's what I found (summary):
- Of the 42 events flagged in Monica's sample, 11 were reprocessed and received new processed_ts values but kept the same usage_id; 4 events were deduplicated and replaced with new usage_id values (these are the three you flagged + one more).
- The deduped records were originally emitted with buyer_entity_id=Acme EU (no VAT) and then re-emitted without buyer_entity_id; the marketplace feed later annotated those records to Acme UK. That flip is the cause of the VAT mismatch.

Action items I recommend:
1) Provide Acme the origin -> processed mapping CSV for the affected usage_ids (include marketplace_sequence_id, origin_ts, processed_ts, usage_id_old, usage_id_new).
2) If Acme prefers, we can issue a corrective credit memo for the three deduped usage lines and update our payout ledger; attach proposed credit memo template.
3) Pause any automated cash allocation for invoices tied to those usage_ids until we confirm final entity attribution.

Attaching the event-diff export as a zip: (attachment: event-diff-2027-02-28.zip)

Jonas
Engineering — Billing Systems
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme-corp.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed settlement path for Feb marketplace delta

Alice / team —

Thanks for routing the Acme export. Based on Jonas' diff and Monica's ledger snapshot, here's a suggested operational path to close this quickly:

1) Redwood issues a one-time corrective credit memo for the three deduped usage lines (total: EUR 18,742.90). We'll generate an updated payout ledger row and label it "marketplace-dedup-credit-2027-02".
2) Acme can accept the credit (we'll apply it against March 2027 invoice) or request a separate refund — either is fine, but please confirm preference.
3) Both parties retain the origin vs processed mapping CSV as audit evidence for VAT filings; Acme should attach our mapping to their VAT return if they choose the credit route.
4) We'll add a short note to both parties' ledgers describing the ingestion window and root cause (connector backlog + reprocessing cascade).

If that path is acceptable, I'll coordinate with Finance to draft the credit memo and DocuSign the acceptance/settlement term sheet. Chloe — can you confirm internal approval to issue the credit?

Best,
Marissa
Head of Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0199
(attachment: proposed-settlement-term-sheet-2027-03-03.pdf)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposed settlement path for Feb marketplace delta

All —

Approved to proceed with the credit memo path. Please generate the credit memo and term sheet for signature. Alice, if Acme confirms applying the credit against Mar 2027 invoice that will be quickest for both sides. Otherwise we can process a refund — either option is fine.

For audit purposes, please include the origin -> processed mapping and the AWS marketplace sequence exports in the DocuSign package (we'll keep copies in our compliance folder).

Next steps:
- Marissa to create credit memo + DocuSign envelope (target: Fri 2027-03-05 EOD PT).
- Monica will upload the ledger snapshot and event-diff CSV to the HubSpot record.
- Jonas to pause automated cash allocation for the impacted invoice lines.

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

Chloe
